{"id": "codex-51152", "titulo": "app-server rejects every turn with \"invalid cwd\" once the daemon's own working directory is deleted, even when the request cwd is absolute", "texto": "## What happens\n\nThe shared app-server daemon starts with the working directory of the first `codex` invocation that spawns it. If that directory is later deleted (a removed git worktree, for example), every new `turn/start` on that daemon fails:\n\n```\nturn/start failed: invalid cwd: No such file or directory (os error 2) (code -32600)\n```\n\nThis happens even though the turn's own `cwd` is an absolute path to a directory that exists. Every TUI attached to the daemon is affected until the daemon restarts. `codex resume <thread> --no-daemon` works around it for one session.\n\n## Why\n\n`resolve_request_cwd` (codex-rs/app-server/src/request_processors.rs:629, rust-v0.160.0) resolves the request cwd with `AbsolutePathBuf::relative_to_current_dir`:\n\n```rust\nfn resolve_request_cwd(cwd: Option<PathBuf>) -> Result<Option<AbsolutePathBuf>, JSONRPCErrorError> {\n    cwd.map(|cwd| {\n        AbsolutePathBuf::relative_to_current_dir(path_utils::normalize_for_native_workdir(cwd))\n            .map_err(|err| invalid_request(format!(\"invalid cwd: {err}\")))\n    })\n    .transpose()\n}\n```\n\n`relative_to_current_dir` (codex-rs/utils/absolute-path/src/lib.rs:87) calls `std::env::current_dir()?` unconditionally, before it looks at whether `path` is already absolute:\n\n```rust\npub fn relative_to_current_dir<P: AsRef<Path>>(path: P) -> std::io::Result<Self> {\n    Ok(Self::resolve_path_against_base(\n        path,\n        std::env::current_dir()?,\n    ))\n}\n```\n\nOn Linux, `getcwd` fails with ENOENT when the process's cwd has been unlinked. So an absolute request path is rejected because of the daemon's own cwd, which the path does not depend on. The same call is used for `turn/start` (turn_processor.rs:621, :928) and thread resume (thread_processor.rs:3877).\n\n## Reproduce\n\n1. With no daemon running (`codex app-server daemon stop`), run `mkdir /tmp/x && cd /tmp/x && codex`. This starts the daemon with cwd `/tmp/x`. Exit the TUI.\n2. `rm -rf /tmp/x`\n3. `cd ~/some/repo && codex`, then send any prompt. The turn fails with `invalid cwd`.\n\n## Expected\n\nAn absolute request cwd resolves without consulting the process cwd. Only a relative request cwd needs `current_dir()`, and its error could say that the daemon's working directory no longer exists.\n\nPossible fix: in `relative_to_current_dir`, return `from_absolute_path(path)` when `path.is_absolute()`, and call `current_dir()` only for relative input.\n\n## Related\n\nThe managed daemon and its updater both inherit the spawning terminal's cwd (`codex app-server daemon start`, and `Daemon::stop` leaves `daemon-updater.pid` running). So after `stop` + `start`, the next update recreates the daemon in the deleted directory again; only `daemon bootstrap` replaces both processes. Starting the managed daemon from a stable directory (for example `$CODEX_HOME`) regardless of the caller's cwd would remove the whole class.\n\nEnvironment: codex-cli 0.160.0 (npm, linux-x64 musl), Ubuntu, managed app-server daemon (`codex app-server --listen unix:// --managed-daemon`).\n\nRelated report: #41559 (a session whose own cwd was removed). This issue is a different trigger: the request cwd exists and is absolute, and only the daemon process's cwd is gone.\n"}

This appears consistent with the observed behavior; it is a source-based hypothesis rather than proof about the exact release binary.\n\nAn isolated/fresh app-server accepts the corrected config. The command fails with `helper_unknown_error: setup refresh had errors`.\n\n### What is the expected behavior?\n\nWhen the ACL is already correct, setup refresh should not need write access to runtime files, and commands should run.\n\n### Additional information\n\n**Proposed fix (tested):** https://github.com/erson/codex/commit/2bd3cd554dd26b40078265df121ca7546981bb58\n\n- Read the DACL through `fetch_dacl_handle` (a `READ_CONTROL` handle) for both root-only and inheriting grants.\n- Open the `MAXIMUM_ALLOWED` handle only when at least one ACE must be written. That keeps the no-propagation behavior from #49690.\n- Add the regression test `noninheriting_grant_skips_open_for_write_when_ace_is_present`. It holds a read-only-sharing handle on the target, like a loaded image, and checks that an up-to-date root-only grant succeeds.\n\nI tried to open a pull request, but the repository does not accept external PRs, so the commit is linked here instead.\n\n**Testing.** The computer-use helper held the runtime files during all end-to-end runs. Observe repeated `maybe_resume_skipped_inactive_hotkey_window` log events and high CPU/memory usage.\n5. Closing only the hidden Pages window causes `PageWindowPrewarm` to create a replacement, which immediately resumes the same loop. Restarting the app also reproduced it on this installation.\n\nSession identifiers and raw conversation contents are omitted from this public report.\n\n### What is the expected behavior?\n\nA hidden Pages prewarm renderer should not request conversation resume when acquiring the thread stream is prohibited. A normal `not-ready / inactive-window` response should not cause an unbounded retry loop. Recreating or restarting the prewarm window should not restart the loop.\n\n### Additional information\n\n### Runtime correlation\n\nTemporarily suspending only the replacement prewarm renderer stopped the repeated logs while the main window and chat continued to work. During a 138-second observation, there were zero new repetitions and ordinary app logging continued. This is a temporary workaround, not a permanent fix.\n\n### Suggested fix direction\n\nAlign the resume-needed predicate with the prewarm ownership guard and handle `not-ready` responses with an appropriate retry policy. An isolated local candidate changed the shared predicate to:\n\n```js\nfunction ari(e,t){return !eHn()&&(e==null||e===`needs_resume`||t==null)}\n```\n\nThe extracted-function checks passed 123 assertions, and the modified module passed Node syntax checking. **The candidate was not installed. This report adds concrete `logs_2.sqlite` connection-manager evidence and a same-machine CLI control test.\n\n## Environment\n\n- OS: Windows x64, `10.0.19041` (Windows 10)\n- Codex Desktop: `OpenAI.Codex` MSIX package **`26.1002.7124.0`**, status `Ok` (`Get-AppxPackage -Name OpenAI.Codex`)\n- Codex binary bundled with Desktop: **`0.162.0-alpha.2`** (reported by `codex.exe exec`)\n- Server: `vibe-monitor` custom stdio MCP\n- MCP runtime: bundled Node.js **`22.23.3`**, Windows x64\n- Server software: **Vibe Monitor `0.3.0-beta.26`**\n- User-level configuration: `%USERPROFILE%\\.codex\\config.toml`\n\nSanitized relevant config:\n\n```toml\nmcp_optional_startup_grace_ms = 0\n\n[mcp_servers.vibe-monitor]\nenabled = true\nstartup_timeout_sec = 30\ncommand = \"C:\\\\Users\\\\<USER>\\\\.vibe-monitor\\\\bin\\\\vibe-monitor.cmd\"\nargs = [\"mcp\", \"--agent\", \"codex\"]\n\n[mcp_servers.vibe-monitor.tools.vibe_version]\napproval_mode = \"approve\"\n\n[mcp_servers.vibe-monitor.tools.vibe_session_start]\napproval_mode = \"approve\"\n```\n\nThe initial issue reproduced prior to adding the startup grace and 30-second timeout options; adding them did **not** restore the missing Desktop tools.\n\n## Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Register and enable `vibe-monitor` as a stdio MCP server in the user Codex config.\n2. Confirm that `codex.exe mcp get vibe-monitor` reports:\n   ```text\n   enabled: true\n   transport: stdio\n   command: C:\\Users\\<USER>\\.vibe-monitor\\bin\\vibe-monitor.cmd\n   args: mcp --agent codex\n   startup_timeout_sec: 30\n   ```\n3. Start Codex Desktop and open a Desktop chat/task. Inspect `/mcp` and request `vibe_version` or `vibe_session_start`. The tools are not available to the task, despite an MCP process having been launched.\n4. Check Desktop's `%USERPROFILE%\\.codex\\logs_2.sqlite` read-only: see the successful initialization and catalog messages below.\n5. As a control, invoke the Codex binary independently in a read-only sandbox:\n   ```cmd\n   \"<PATH_TO_CODEX_EXE>\\codex.exe\" exec --skip-git-repo-check --sandbox read-only -C \"<TEST_REPO>\" \"Actually call the vibe-monitor MCP tool vibe_version and report its result; do not edit files.\"\n   ```\n6. Observe that this independent CLI run successfully calls both `vibe-monitor/vibe_session_start` and `vibe-monitor/vibe_version`, with the latter returning `0.3.0-beta.26`.\n\n## Actual behavior\n\n- Desktop chat/task has no usable Vibe Monitor MCP tools.\n- The stdio server is **enabled** in the effective CLI config; both launcher and runtime files exist.\n- Desktop's MCP client initializes the server and the aggregate connection-manager catalog reports **no unavailable MCP servers**.\n- Running the same configured MCP from the independent CLI succeeds.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\nA successfully initialized, enabled custom stdio MCP server's callable tools should be exposed to new Codex Desktop tasks. If a specific tool is excluded by a tool-budget/filtering/approval policy, Desktop should make that reason discoverable, rather than silently leaving the tool unavailable.\n\n## Evidence from Desktop diagnostics\n\nRead-only query of `%USERPROFILE%\\.codex\\logs_2.sqlite`:\n\n```text\n[4509] INFO rmcp::service\nnew{server_name=vibe-monitor}:start_server_task{server_name=vibe-monitor}:serve_inner:\nService initialized as client peer_info=Some(ServerPeerInfo {\n  protocol_version: ProtocolVersion(\"2025-06-18\"),\n  capabilities: ... tools: Some(...)\n})\n\n[4510] TRACE codex_mcp::connection_manager::tool_catalog\nlist_tools_with_errors{mcp_server_count=6}:\nbuilt MCP tool list available_server_count=6 unavailable_server_count=0 tool_count=886\n\n[4517] INFO rmcp::service\nnew{server_name=vibe-monitor}:start_server_task{server_name=vibe-monitor}:serve_inner:\ntask cancelled\n\n[4521] INFO rmcp::service\nnew{server_name=vibe-monitor}:start_server_task{server_name=vibe-monitor}:serve_inner:\nserve finished quit_reason=Cancelled\n```\n\nNotes on interpreting these logs:\n\n- `tool_count=886` is the **aggregate** tool count across all available servers; it does not independently prove that every Vibe Monitor tool was admitted to this particular Desktop task.\n- The `Cancelled` shutdown messages occurred for multiple servers (`node_repl`, `cua_repl`, `codex_app`, etc.) in the same block, not just Vibe Monitor, so they **do not establish** a Vibe Monitor-specific crash.\n- A filtered query for recent `WARN`/`ERROR` logs and `codex_mcp::connection_manager::tool_catalog` records produced only the successful catalog line above.\n\n## Independent CLI control — works\n\n```text\nOpenAI Codex v0.162.0-alpha.2\nsandbox: read-only\n\nmcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_session_start started\nmcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_session_start (completed)\nmcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_version started\nmcp: vibe-monitor/vibe_version (completed)\n\nVibe Monitor version: 0.3.0-beta.26\n```\n\nIndependent telemetry confirms a fresh `codex` invocation ran the actual compiled `0.3.0-beta.26` client (rather than only reading an installer version pointer), completed a full scan in 16 ms, and successfully reported the result to the server.\n\n## Request\n\nCould the Codex maintainers investigate the gap between **MCP initialization / aggregate tool-catalog creation** and the **tools actually injected into a new Windows Desktop task** in package `26.1002.7124.0` / runtime `0.162.0-alpha.2`?\n\nIs `tool_count=886` expected to trigger a tool-selection limit, deferred-loading path, or per-task filtering that can silently omit tools from an otherwise healthy server?\n\nNo credentials, personal paths, session identifiers, device identifiers, or database contents are included in this report."}

{"id": "codex-52642", "titulo": "[TUI] “This server is not managed by Codex” obscures daemon ownership and safe recovery", "texto": "## Summary\n\nWhen the TUI finds a reachable shared app-server with incompatible feature flags, it can disable **Restart with these settings** with:\n\n```text\nThis server is not managed by Codex.\n```\n\nThis message is misleading. The condition checked is whether the **Codex app-server daemon manager recognizes the running backend**, not whether the server was launched by a Codex client. Codex Desktop/CLI can launch an app-server that is not owned by that particular daemon manager. The message sounds like the user has started an external server and does not explain what prevents a restart or how to recover safely.\n\nThis issue focuses on the **TUI diagnostic and recovery choices**. It does not propose adopting or force-restarting a process without established ownership.\n\n## Observed behavior\n\nIn the shared-server feature-mismatch case reported on Linux with Codex CLI 0.161.0 (see #52085), starting plain `codex` showed:\n\n```text\nBackground server has incompatible feature settings\nThis session requires api_key_model_discovery to be enabled\n\nRestart will use these shared feature settings:\n  api_key_model_discovery = true\n  auth_elicitation = true\n  code_mode_host = true\n  mcp_oauth_refresh_coordination = false\n```\n\nThe **Restart with these settings** choice was disabled with `This server is not managed by Codex.`, leaving **Run without daemon this time** and **Cancel**.\n\nThe user had not manually started an external app-server and was using Codex clients. The precise process launch path/ownership on that host was not independently captured, so this report does **not** assert an incorrect ownership classification.\n\nA non-disruptive recovery **was** confirmed: `codex --disable api_key_model_discovery` (or persisting `[features] api_key_model_discovery = false` in `~/.codex/config.toml`) allowed plain `codex` to attach to the *existing* server, with ChatGPT authentication, without restarting the server or interrupting other work. That option was not disclosed in the TUI.\n\n## Code path\n\nThe wording is directly traceable to:\n\n1. [`app-server-daemon/src/lib.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/47b80571f0d6587060a580c47f6af0cfaefb0d5c/codex-rs/app-server-daemon/src/lib.rs#L409-L427): an app-server can answer the socket probe while `running_backend(&settings)` returns `None`.\n2. [`tui/src/startup_orchestration.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/47b80571f0d6587060a580c47f6af0cfaefb0d5c/codex-rs/tui/src/startup_orchestration.rs#L542-L573): `managed_daemon = output.backend.is_some()`.\n3. [`tui/src/daemon_recovery.rs`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/47b80571f0d6587060a580c47f6af0cfaefb0d5c/codex-rs/tui/src/daemon_recovery.rs#L159-L170): the disabled restart choice translates `!managed_daemon` to `\"This server is not managed by Codex.\"`.\n\nAs a result, the UI turns a narrowly defined daemon-management check into a broad statement about “Codex” without disclosing the actual failed criterion.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\n- Use precise terminology, for example: **“The app-server is reachable, but the Codex app-server daemon manager does not recognize it as a managed instance. Automatic restart is unavailable.”**\n- Distinguish **server reachability**, **daemon-managed lifecycle ownership**, and **who originally launched the server**. Do not imply a proven launch origin where none was established.\n- When the incompatibility is an optional feature flag, show a non-disruptive client-side alternative where applicable (for this case, `codex --disable api_key_model_discovery`), including that it keeps using the existing shared server. Do not present `--no-daemon` as the only non-restart option.\n- If useful, point to a read-only daemon-status check and the specific missing management evidence. Continue to refuse potentially disruptive restarts of unowned processes.\n\n## Related, but separate\n\n- #52085 / #51891: feature-default mismatch involving `api_key_model_discovery`.\n- #49612: Desktop SSH process/lifecycle ambiguity and unclear recovery.\n- #37893: a reachable app-server becoming unmanaged after daemon state loss.\n- #24542: Codex Desktop remote proxy starting an app-server outside the managed-daemon lifecycle.\n\nThese concern feature compatibility or process lifecycle. This report is specifically about the **misleading TUI diagnosis and absent safe recovery guidance**, which also applies when unmanaged process status is intentional.\n"}

Directory masks (`--tmpfs`) are not affected.\n"}

When `download_file_with_fallback` subsequently downloads the actual package archive (`codex-package-*.tar.gz`), it writes directly to `$archive_path`—which is `$checksum_path`! The package archive completely overwrites and destroys the checksum manifest file on disk.\n2. The package archive is never saved under its real name (`codex-package-$vendor_target.tar.gz`).\n3. If an archive download fails or encounters an error without writing (or if fallback occurs), `verify_archive_digest` verifies `$checksum_path` (which still contains the checksum manifest text), resulting in bogus checksum mismatch errors:\n   `Downloaded Codex archive checksum did not match expected digest.`\n   (as previously reported in #49337).\n\n### What steps can reproduce the bug?\n\nRun a minimal script tracing `archive_path` before and after downloading the checksum manifest:\n\n```sh\nsh -c '\ntmp_dir=\"/tmp/test_sh_bug\"\nasset=\"codex-package-darwin.tar.gz\"\nchecksum_asset=\"codex-package_SHA256SUMS\"\n\nverify_archive_digest() {\n  archive_path=\"$1\"\n}\n\narchive_path=\"$tmp_dir/$asset\"\nchecksum_path=\"$tmp_dir/$checksum_asset\"\n\necho \"BEFORE checksum download: archive_path=$archive_path\"\nverify_archive_digest \"$checksum_path\"\necho \"AFTER  checksum download: archive_path=$archive_path\"\n'\n```\n\nOutput:\n```\nBEFORE checksum download: archive_path=/tmp/test_sh_bug/codex-package-darwin.tar.gz\nAFTER  checksum download: archive_path=/tmp/test_sh_bug/codex-package_SHA256SUMS\n```\n\nThe destination of the package archive is permanently clobbered into the checksum manifest path.\n\n### What is the expected behavior?\n\n`verify_archive_digest` should use a local parameter name (`archive_file=\"$1\"`) so it does not overwrite the global `archive_path` variable.\nThe checksum manifest and the package archive should be downloaded into two distinct files, and the checksum manifest must remain intact.\n\n### Additional information\n\nRelated issue: #49337\n\nWe have prepared a tested fix on a fork branch and opened a pull request on the fork (since openai/codex restricts external pull requests):\n- **Pull Request on fork:** https://github.com/Saauf/codex/pull/1\n- **Commit:** [706b01d](https://github.com/Saauf/codex/commit/706b01d44a0173e4d2f091fe5e3c26681b530ede)\n- **Branch:** `fix/install-sh-archive-path-clobbering`\n\nThe fix:\n1. Renames `archive_path` to `archive_file` in `verify_archive_digest()`.\n2. Renames `asset` to `target_asset` in `package_archive_digest()` to avoid variable collision.\n3. Adds an automated test in `scripts/install/test_install_sh.py` (`test_package_archive_download_does_not_overwrite_checksum_manifest`) verifying both files are downloaded to distinct destinations.\n\nMaintainers can cherry-pick this fix with:\n```bash\ngit fetch https://github.com/Saauf/codex.git fix/install-sh-archive-path-clobbering\ngit cherry-pick 706b01d44a0173e4d2f091fe5e3c26681b530ede\n```\n"}

{"id": "codex-53298", "titulo": "codex-utils-pty: let a caller observe an exited PTY child before the waiter reaps it", "texto": "### What variant of Codex are you using?\n\nThe `codex-utils-pty` Rust crate, used as a library dependency at `rust-v0.154.0`.\n\n### What feature would you like to see?\n\nAn opt-in, bounded way to look at an exited PTY child before `codex-utils-pty` reaps it.\n\nToday both Unix PTY spawn paths (`spawn_process_portable` and `spawn_process_preserving_fds` in `utils/pty/src/pty.rs`) reap the child in their own waiter as soon as it exits. That is the right default, and the waiter must stay the only reaper. But a caller that accounts for a launch by its process group cannot inspect the group while the exited root still holds its PID and process group ID. Once the root is reaped, a descendant that ignored SIGHUP and stayed in the group can no longer be attributed with certainty, because the ID may be reused. The caller cannot reap the child itself, and a second waiter would race the existing one.\n\nProposed shape (implemented in the reference patch below):\n\n- `spawn_pty_process_observed(program, args, cwd, env, arg0, size, inherited_fds, observer)`, the same as `spawn_pty_process` plus an `observe::ExitObserver { opportunity: oneshot::Sender<ExitOpportunity>, bound: Duration, outcome: oneshot::Sender<ObservationOutcome> }`. The observer is registered before the spawn, so even a very fast exit cannot be missed.\n- When the child exits, the existing waiter calls `waitid(P_PID, pid, WEXITED | WNOWAIT)`. The child stays a zombie and keeps its PID and process group ID.\n- The waiter then publishes one `ExitOpportunity`, which carries no PID, and waits until it is acknowledged or the bound passes. Only then does it reap through the original child object, exactly as today.\n- After the reap, and before the exit code is sent, it reports one of:\n  - `Completed`;\n  - `TimedOut`;\n  - `Failed`, when the observer dropped the opportunity or stopped listening;\n  - `Unavailable`, when the exit could not be seen without reaping.\n\n  An `acknowledge()` after the bound returns `OpportunityExpired`.\n- Without an observer, nothing changes: `spawn_pty_process` and every existing path are untouched. Platforms other than Unix refuse an observed spawn before creating a process.\n\nThe bound keeps every failure finite. A stalled observer delays the reap by at most the bound, and a dropped one ends the wait at once. Termination and handle Drop during the window still reach the process group, which the unreaped child keeps, and the child is reaped exactly once.\n\n### Additional information\n\n- Reference implementation: a patch to `rust-v0.154.0`, one commit exported with `git format-patch`: https://github.com/novelKR/CodeSpace/blob/374a3fc6f9897ce97d1eb9b442df8d0f627aba08/third_party/codex-patches/0001-utils-pty-pre-reap-observation.patch. It is 304 added and 5 removed lines of product code (`observe.rs`, `pty.rs`, `lib.rs`) plus nine tests, each run on both Unix paths. The tests cover:\n  - the exit seen before the reap;\n  - the bound, including a late acknowledgement refused;\n  - a dropped opportunity and a dropped observer;\n  - a SIGHUP-ignoring descendant still in the root's process group during the window;\n  - termination in the window;\n  - a handle dropped in the window;\n  - 256 KiB of output draining fully;\n  - a runtime shutdown held only for the bound.\n- Verified on Linux x86_64 (36 crate tests) and macOS (38; two existing tests are macOS-only): every test passes in each of 30 repeated runs, and clippy is clean on Linux, macOS and Windows targets. On macOS we also ran it under our resource manager: a surviving descendant stayed attributed to its launch until it ended (10/10), a stalled observer was reaped at its 500 ms bound, and the observer added about 4 ms at the median to the exit report.\n- `ProcessDriver` / `spawn_from_driver` would make the caller own PTY allocation, terminal setup, I/O and reaping, duplicating this crate. A hook inside the existing single waiter avoids that.\n- CodeSpace has used it for its governed PTY executions since 2026-10-12 (https://github.com/novelKR/CodeSpace/pull/95): the resource manager observes the exited root's process group in the window, so a descendant that outlives its root stays attributed to its launch until it ends.\n- We carry this as a downstream patch and will drop it once an upstream equivalent exists. Any API shape that keeps the single waiter, a bound and an outcome would meet our need.\n"}

its text contains a single copy.\n- The duplicate is a TUI rendering artifact: the preamble was streamed, then an exec call (`call_01_rVU62B0h7dFC4uFva2bX5570`, `call_00_hBkMrELAYk5zDGynIyiS9053`) interleaved before the message item completed.\n\n### Root cause (with code pointers)\n\n1. The model streams the preamble as `AgentMessageDelta`; it accumulates in `stream_controller`.\n2. Before the message item completes, a tool/exec call starts. `on_command_execution_started` calls `flush_answer_stream_with_separator()`, which finalizes the partial stream and consolidates it into scrollback:\n   - `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/streaming.rs:22` (`flush_answer_stream_with_separator`)\n   - `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/command_lifecycle.rs:33` (exec start → flush)\n3. The guard in `finalize_completed_assistant_message` only checks whether the stream controller is idle — which it now is — so it re-injects the entire text as a brand-new stream:\n   ```rust\n   // codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/streaming.rs:127\n   pub(super) fn finalize_completed_assistant_message(&mut self, message: Option<&str>) {\n       if self.stream_controller.is_none()\n           && let Some(message) = message\n           && !message.is_empty()\n       {\n           self.handle_streaming_delta(message.to_string()); // second copy of the same text\n       }\n       ...\n   }\n   ```\n\nSo the same message is rendered once by the streamed partial flush and again by item completion, which is exactly the \"text → `Ran` → same text\" shape in the screenshot. Item completion should only re-inject content when the streamed text was actually dropped/truncated (i.e. when it differs from what was already consolidated), not when it matches an already-consolidated partial flush.\n\n### Additional information\n\n- The related guard is also present on current upstream `origin/main`, so this likely still needs fixing there.\n- Suggested fix (verified locally): record the source consolidated by a non-authoritative partial flush and skip re-injection at item completion when it matches:\n  - `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/streaming.rs` (guard in `finalize_completed_assistant_message`, bookkeeping in `flush_answer_stream`)\n  - `codex-rs/tui/src/chatwidget/transcript.rs` (`last_flushed_agent_message` state, reset in `reset_turn_flags`)\n- Full `chatwidget::tests` suite passes with the fix (789 passed), including the existing dropped-delta repair test `live_app_server_turn_completion_repairs_dropped_message_deltas`.\n"}

The Codex rendering failure was discovered during this update period.\n\nBecause both the Codex application and Windows were updated nearly simultaneously, it has not been established which update introduced the problem or whether an interaction between them is responsible.\n\nThe malfunction persists after the Windows updates completed and after multiple system restarts.\n\n**Other application behavior:**\n\n- Opera and other applications appear to function normally.\n- GPU-accelerated video playback through YouTube and Rumble operates without observable problems.\n- Windows Terminal and PowerShell function normally.\n- A briefly observed blue PowerShell banner was identified as the normal `Get-ComputerInfo` progress indicator, not a rendering artifact.\n- Codex continues to display raw CSS even when launched with `--disable-gpu`.\n\n**Diagnostic conclusion:**\n\nThe near-simultaneous Windows 11 26H2 and Codex updates introduce the possibility of an application/operating-system compatibility regression.\n\nNo specific Windows update has been established as the cause. The problem remains reproducible under two separate Windows user accounts.\n\n## Problem description\n\nFollowing the most recent Codex update, approximately October 13–14, 2026, the application became unusable.\n\nWhen launched, the main application window immediately displays raw CSS source text instead of the normal Codex interface.\n\nThe CSS fills the window, including the custom title-bar/frame region. It initially appears dimmed during window opening, then becomes fully visible.\n\nThe text is selectable and dynamically reflows when the window is resized.\n\nThe problem persists after restarting Windows, using Windows Repair, and launching Codex under a separate Windows user account.\n\n## Actual behavior\n\nThe displayed text begins:\n\n```css\n/* Dependency CSS can load before app.css, so establish Tailwind's layer order here. */\n@layer theme, base, components, utilities;\n\n:root {\n  --startup-background: transparent;\n  --startup-logo-shimmer-base: rgb(0 0 0 / 0.24);\n  --startup-logo-shimmer-peak: rgb(255 255 255 / 0.48);\n```\n\nThe displayed text continues through extensive CSS declarations, including application styling and theme definitions, and ends with:\n\n```css\n:host { display: flex; }\n```\n\nThe window title is `ChatGPT`.\n\nAdditional observations:\n\n- The CSS text is selectable, but there is no visible text insertion cursor.\n- Resizing or maximizing the window causes the CSS text to reflow.\n- The CSS occupies the main interface, including the custom window-frame region.\n- Normal project content is not visible underneath the CSS.\n- Some project-editing interface elements appear intermingled with the CSS text.\n- Project-editing text responds to mouse hover and displays tooltips.\n- The project `...` menu renders normally above the CSS.\n- The Rename dialog also renders normally above the CSS.\n- Selecting a project through the system tray does not produce a usable project workspace.\n- `Ctrl+R` produces no visible change.\n- `Ctrl+Shift+I` does not open Developer Tools.\n\nThe behavior suggests that the application's main window is partially functional, but stylesheet content is being exposed as visible text.\n\n## Expected behavior\n\nCodex should display its normal project and conversation interface, with CSS applied as styling rather than rendered as document text.\n\nExisting projects and conversations should remain accessible.\n\n## Steps to reproduce\n\n1. Open the project-editing menu, where available.\n5. Observe that the menu and Rename dialog render normally above the malformed main interface.\n\nThe failure was reproduced under two separate Windows user accounts on the same computer.\n\nUnder the second account, a three-option dialog containing Logout and Cancel appeared normally before the main window displayed the same CSS problem. No display driver or VM hardware change was needed for the eventual workaround.\n\nThis is an additional reproduction of the Windows 10 capture failure family, with a before/after test that also covers coordinate input. Related reports: #25178, #35446, #46435, and #51245. In particular, the [October 14 exact-build workaround report](https://github.com/openai/codex/issues/25178#issuecomment-6169771678) matches the original helper hash below. This report does not claim a newly discovered root cause or an official fix.\n\n### What steps can reproduce the bug?\n\n1. Open a blank, unminimized `Untitled - Notepad` window on the affected Windows 10 installation.\n2. Use the normal Computer Use plugin through `node_repl` and `@oai/sky`.\n3. Select the unique returned Notepad window and request a screenshot:\n\n```js\nconst { sky } = await import('@oai/sky');\nconst apps = await sky.list_apps();\nconst matches = apps.flatMap(a => a.windows)\n  .filter(w => /^Untitled - Notepad$/i.test(w.title ?? ''));\nif (matches.length !== 1) throw new Error('Expected one Notepad window');\nconst selected = matches[0];\nconst window = await sky.get_window({ id: selected.id, app: selected.app });\nawait sky.activate_window({ window });\nawait sky.get_window_state({\n  window,\n  include_screenshot: true,\n  include_text: true,\n});\n```\n\nScreenshot requests repeatedly time out. Text-only observations succeed.\n\n### What is the expected behavior?\n\nThe normal native Computer Use plugin should return screenshots and usable coordinate geometry for Notepad, allowing clicks and text input without a local binary patch.\n\n### Additional information: isolation, workaround, and validation\n\n**Independent Windows capture test:** A temporary C++/WinRT test used `CreateForWindow`, `Direct3D11CaptureFramePool::CreateFreeThreaded`, `StartCapture`, and `TryGetNextFrame` against the same blank Notepad window. It obtained a **1030 × 781** frame with both hardware selection (which resolved to Microsoft Basic Render Driver) and WARP. `GraphicsCaptureSession::IsSupported()` was true and the reported device/capture setup HRESULTs were `0x00000000`. Thus Windows capture could produce a frame while the stock helper timed out. This test alone does not prove every bitmap-conversion dependency inside the helper.\n\n**Exact helper identity:** `codex-computer-use.exe` under the bundled `@oai/sky/bin/windows` runtime:\n\n```text\nOriginal SHA-256:\nD36AE6626BDCED7AE07935D1A91BE14425E8F6CE7C9B5C69F2D8D7DF0C130D83\n\nPatched SHA-256:\n452E61A51C24273F22280ACA8A7216B26F077F1683D4A3D9F87487577DBC299B\n```\n\n**Workaround applied:** We adapted the existing [community patch](https://github.com/chen0416ccc-cpu/codex-windows-fast-patch-skill) to this exact original binary, following the linked October 14 report. The candidate matched that report's patched SHA-256 exactly. It redirects the `FrameArrived` delegate through a wrapper that atomically claims the once flag, retains the delegate, starts an MTA worker, and returns promptly. The worker initializes WinRT, executes the original callback body, uninitializes WinRT, and releases the delegate. Thread-creation failure restores the flag/reference count. Associated guard branches, the vtable entry, a new executable section, and x64 unwind metadata are updated.\n\nThe explanation supported by the existing investigations is a circular wait: synchronous bitmap-conversion waiting inside the frame callback prevents the callback from returning, while conversion completion on the affected Windows 10 path needs it to return. Our successful patch test is consistent with that explanation; we did not independently obtain source-level traces proving the entire dependency chain.\n\nFor this exact build, the patch has **13 regions** and **does not include an optional-border-interface bypass**. Independent static review checked all changed bytes against the manifest, imported call destinations, callback/reference handling, section layout, retained ASLR relocation, and unwind records. The verified original was backed up before atomic replacement, and a hash-guarded rollback script was retained. No auth, permission, network, VM hardware, or display-driver changes were made as part of this fix.\n\n**Important limitation:** This modifies a vendor-signed executable and invalidates its original Authenticode signature. It is a local community workaround, not an official release or a recommendation to patch arbitrary builds; an update may overwrite it.\n\n**Actual post-patch acceptance through the normal plugin:**\n\n- Multiple `sky.get_window_state` calls with screenshots succeeded.\n- `sky.click` with fresh `screenshotId` and screenshot coordinates clicked the blank Notepad editor successfully.\n- `sky.type_text` entered `test`; the Windows chat verified it appeared.\n- Keyboard input erased the disposable text; a subsequent screenshot/accessibility observation confirmed the document was blank again.\n\nThe test used the existing plugin and native helper path, not the standalone C++ capture test or an alternate automation backend. {"id": "codex-54599", "titulo": "`$HOME/.codex` is loaded as a project config layer when `CODEX_HOME` points somewhere else (follow-up to #9932)", "texto": "### What version of Codex is running?\n\ncodex-cli 0.163.0, the latest release. Also reproduced on 0.160.1. Current `main` has the same check.\n\n### What platform is your computer?\n\nLinux x86_64\n\n### What issue are you seeing?\n\nRun Codex with `CODEX_HOME` set to a directory other than `$HOME/.codex`, and with the working directory at `$HOME`. The default home folder `$HOME/.codex` is then discovered as a **project** `.codex` layer.\n\nThe project root falls back to cwd when no `.git` marker is found. If `$HOME` is a trusted project, the whole `config.toml` of that other home applies to the session, and it applies with project precedence, above the active user config. That covers:\n\n- model, approval and personality settings;\n- MCP servers;\n- hooks from `$HOME/.codex/hooks.json`;\n- skills under `$HOME/.codex/skills`;\n- plugin enablement;\n- marketplace sources and MCP env values that point into the other home's directories.\n\nIf `$HOME` is not trusted, you get the \"config folders are disabled\" warning from #9932 instead.\n\nSeen through the app-server, `config/read` with `{\"cwd\": \"<HOME>\", \"includeLayers\": true}` lists `{\"type\": \"project\", \"dotCodexFolder\": \"<HOME>/.codex\"}` above the `user` layer for `<CODEX_HOME>/config.toml`. The `origins` show the project layer winning keys that the active home also sets.\n\nPR #10207 fixed #9932 by skipping a discovered `.codex` folder only when it **is** the active `CODEX_HOME`. Here is the check in `codex-rs/config/src/loader/mod.rs`, in the project-layer discovery loop:\n\n```rust\nif dot_codex_abs == codex_home_abs || dot_codex_normalized == codex_home_normalized {\n    continue;\n}\n```\n\nWhen `CODEX_HOME` is a different directory, `$HOME/.codex` no longer matches, and it is treated as an ordinary project folder.\n\nThis matters whenever two Codex installs share one machine but keep separate homes. One example is an app or editor integration with its own `CODEX_HOME`, next to a CLI that uses the default `~/.codex`. Any session or thread whose cwd is `$HOME` silently picks up the other install's configuration. Sessions started anywhere else don't, so the same install behaves differently depending only on its working directory.\n\n### What steps can reproduce the bug?\n\nThis uses a throwaway `HOME`, so your real config is not touched:\n\n```bash\nt=\"$(mktemp -d)\"\nmkdir -p \"$t/home/.codex\" \"$t/home-b\" \"$t/home/elsewhere\"\n\n# The \"other\" install's home: the default location under HOME.\ncat > \"$t/home/.codex/config.toml\" <<'TOML'\npersonality = \"pragmatic\"\n[mcp_servers.from_default_home]\ncommand = \"true\"\nTOML\n\n# The active install's home: it only trusts HOME as a project.\nprintf '[projects.\"%s/home\"]\\ntrust_level = \"trusted\"\\n' \"$t\" > \"$t/home-b/config.toml\"\n\n# cwd = HOME: the other home's config is loaded as a project layer.\n(cd \"$t/home\" && HOME=\"$t/home\" CODEX_HOME=\"$t/home-b\" codex mcp list)\n\n# cwd = a non-git subdirectory of HOME: it is not.\n(cd \"$t/home/elsewhere\" && HOME=\"$t/home\" CODEX_HOME=\"$t/home-b\" codex mcp list)\n```\n\nOutput on 0.163.0:\n\n```\n# cwd = HOME\nName               Command  Args  Env  Cwd  Status   Auth\nfrom_default_home  true     -     -    -    enabled  Unsupported\n\n# cwd = HOME/elsewhere\nNo MCP servers configured yet. Try `codex mcp add my-tool -- my-command`.\n```\n\nThe output also includes a \"could not create PATH aliases\" warning, because the test home sits under `/tmp`. It is unrelated.\n\n### What is the expected behavior?\n\n`$HOME/.codex` is a Codex home location, not a project's config folder. It should not be loaded as a project layer for a session whose `CODEX_HOME` is somewhere else. It should behave the same whether cwd is `$HOME` or any other directory with no project markers.\n\nPossible fixes, whichever fits the loader's design:\n\n- In project-layer discovery, also skip the default home location (`$HOME/.codex`, what `find_codex_home()` resolves to without `CODEX_HOME`), not only the active `CODEX_HOME`.\n- Or never treat a `.codex` folder directly under `$HOME` as a project layer.\n- Or, at minimum, add a config switch that turns project-layer discovery off for a given home, so isolated homes can opt out.\n\n### Additional information\n\nWorkarounds today:\n\n- Start sessions in a directory with no `.git` ancestor other than `$HOME`; the project root then falls back to that directory.\n- Or mark `$HOME` as untrusted. That has wider side effects and brings back the #9932 warning.\n\nRelated: #9932, #10207, #34193 (the converse case, AGENTS.md), #46414 (an isolated `CODEX_HOME` still picks up `$HOME/.agents/skills`).\n"}

{"id": "codex-54897", "titulo": "Async compaction panic leaves the turn stuck inProgress until interrupted", "texto": "### What issue are you seeing?\n\nReproduced with the official `0.164.0-alpha.3` macOS arm64 binary against a loopback Responses backend.\n\nIn [`take_ready()`](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/ce0323f2f2d3b25e82806cd555237da3db4e1897/codex-rs/core/src/session/async_compaction.rs#L144-L180), `try_recv().ok()?` returns on `Closed` without clearing `state.async_compaction.result`. Tokio has already completed that receiver, so a subsequent compatible `wait_for_pending()` panics with `called after complete`.\n\nThe process survives, but the turn remains `inProgress` with `error: null`. No terminal event arrived within 30 seconds; another `turn/start` returned the same turn ID without issuing a model request. `turn/interrupt` followed by a new turn recovers the thread. Other threads remain usable.\n\n### What steps can reproduce the bug?\n\nUsing a mock Responses/SSE backend:\n\n1. Enable async compaction, disable token budget, and enable provider remote compaction V2. Set the context window to 100,000 and auto-compaction limit to 90,000.\n2. Return a normal response reporting 70,000 tokens to start background compaction at the default 65% threshold.\n3. Close the background SSE stream before `response.completed`. Wait for `discarding unsuccessful background compaction` before submitting the next turn.\n4. Return a normal response containing a `list_agents` call and reporting 91,000 tokens. Required foreground compaction then hits the panic.\n\nThe counts and outputs are synthetic; the app-server and session code are unmodified. This also reproduces with `stream_max_retries = 2`, and with an HTTP 400 or missing compaction output instead of a truncated stream.\n\n### What is the expected behavior?\n\nA failed background attempt should allow foreground compaction to proceed without leaving the turn active after its task panics.\n\n### Additional information\n\nSuggested change in `take_ready()`:\n\n```diff\n-    let candidate = state.async_compaction.result.as_mut()?.try_recv().ok()?;\n+    let candidate = match state.async_compaction.result.as_mut()?.try_recv() {\n+        Ok(candidate) => candidate,\n+        Err(oneshot::error::TryRecvError::Empty) => return None,\n+        Err(oneshot::error::TryRecvError::Closed) => {\n+            state.async_compaction.result = None;\n+            return None;\n+        }\n+    };\n     state.async_compaction.result = None;\n```\n\nFor regression coverage, the background failure must complete **before the checkpoint polls it**, rather than while foreground compaction is already waiting.\n"}
